instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In the narratives the thinker is a named person whose thought is quoted: Abraham in Gen 20:11, Isaac in Gen 26:9, Jacob in Gen 31:31 and Gen 32:20, Moses in Exo 2:14, Samuel before Eliab in 1Sa 16:6, Saul toward David in 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:17, 1Sa 18:21, 1Sa 18:25 and 1Sa 20:26, David in 1Sa 27:11, Achish in 1Sa 27:12, Hanun's princes in 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3, Naaman in 2Ki 5:11, Hezekiah in 2Ki 20:19 and Isa 39:8, Sennacherib in 2Ch 32:1, Mordecai to Esther in Est 4:13, Elihu in Job 32:6, Daniel in Dan 4:19 and Dan 7:28.
observations.grounds: I will pin David to the wall

observations.text: In Num 5:28, Judg 13:3, Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23, Luk 1:31 and Heb 11:11 the persons named with conceive are the woman, the child, Immanuel, Jesus and Sarah: they belong to the bodily sense, not to thought.
observations.grounds: the virgin shall conceive and bear a son

observations.text: In Deu 15:9, Jos 22:28, 2Sa 14:17, Job 35:2, Psa 10:4, Psa 48:9, Lam 1:9, Dan 7:25, Jon 1:6, Act 17:29, Rom 1:21, Rom 12:3, 2Cor 10:5, 2Cor 11:3, 1Pe 4:1 and the other verses of this group God, the Lord or Christ is named as the one the thought concerns or is set against (no God in Psa 10:4, the Most High in Dan 7:25, the god who may give a thought in Jon 1:6, the knowledge of God in 2Cor 10:5, Christ in 2Cor 11:3), or the persons named are hearers and brothers addressed.
observations.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

observations.text: The direction runs between God and people: from the Lord who sees, knows and searches the thoughts of man in Gen 6:5, Psa 94:11, Psa 139:23, 1Ch 28:9 and 1Cor 3:20, and who takes thought for the poor in Psa 40:17 and Psa 144:3; and from the Lord's own thoughts toward his people in Psa 40:5, above man's in Isa 55:8 and unknown to the nations in Mic 4:12.
observations.grounds: knows the thoughts of man

observations.text: The direction runs from Jesus into the thoughts of others in Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Luk 5:22 and Luk 6:8, from Jesus asking toward the hearer in Mat 17:25 and Mat 22:42, and from the disciples and the crowd toward Jesus in Joh 11:13, Joh 11:56 and Joh 13:29, where they mistake his meaning.
observations.grounds: But Jesus, knowing their thoughts

observations.text: In the narratives the thought runs from the thinker toward another person or a coming event: Jacob toward Esau in Gen 32:8 and Gen 32:20, Saul toward David in 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:21 and 1Sa 18:25, Achish toward David in 1Sa 27:12, Hanun's princes toward David in 2Sa 10:3, Naaman toward Elisha in 2Ki 5:11, Hezekiah toward his own days in 2Ki 20:19, Sennacherib toward the fortified cities in 2Ch 32:1.
observations.grounds: I will pin David to the wall

observations.text: In Num 5:28, Judg 13:3, Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23, Luk 1:31 and Heb 11:11 no direction of a mind is stated: conceive is bodily, a woman becoming pregnant.
observations.grounds: the virgin shall conceive and bear a son

observations.text: In Deu 15:9, Psa 10:4, Lam 1:9, Dan 7:25, Jon 1:6, Act 17:29, Rom 12:3, 2Cor 10:5, 2Cor 11:3 and the other verses of this group the thought runs from people toward God or away from him (no God in Psa 10:4, against the Most High in Dan 7:25, the god who may give a thought in Jon 1:6, every thought taken captive to Christ in 2Cor 10:5), or toward oneself (Rom 12:3) or toward the hearers addressed.
observations.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

observations.text: In Act 26:8 raising the dead is what is thought incredible: the thought judges God's act unbelievable. In 2Cor 10:5 the proud reasonings set up against knowing God are torn down and every thought is made captive: the raising is of pride against God, and the thought is brought under Christ.
observations.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

observations.text: In Pro 15:26 the Lord abhors the thoughts of the wicked: the thoughts themselves are judged by him. In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future, and her fall is terrible: the lack of thought is followed by the fall.
observations.grounds: The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord

observations.text: In Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 evil thoughts come first in the list of what comes out of the heart, before murder, adultery and the others: the thoughts are the first of the evils that issue from the heart.
observations.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

observations.text: In Psa 40:5 the Lord's wondrous deeds and his thoughts toward his people are named together as many: his thoughts stand with his works.
observations.grounds: your wondrous deeds and your thoughts toward us

observations.text: In 2Ki 5:11 Naaman is angry and goes away saying what he had thought Elisha would do: his anger rises from the thought that was not met.
observations.grounds: But Naaman was angry and went away

observations.text: In Luk 5:22 Jesus perceives their thoughts and asks why they question in their hearts: the thoughts are the questioning within. In Eph 3:20 asking and thinking are joined as what God can do beyond.
observations.grounds: Why do you question in your hearts

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:3 Paul fears the thoughts will be led astray from sincere devotion to Christ, as the serpent deceived Eve: the thoughts are what deceit leads off. In Mat 18:12 astray is the sheep of the parable, asked about with what do you think.
observations.grounds: your thoughts will be led astray

observations.text: In Judg 15:2 the father says he thought Samson hated her and offers the younger, more beautiful sister: the mistaken thought led to the giving, and beauty is his offer in its place.
observations.grounds: Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she

observations.text: In Pro 14:15 the simple believes everything while the prudent gives thought to his steps: believing without weighing is set against thought. In Rom 12:3 sober thinking of oneself is by the measure of faith God gives. In Phili 3:4 and Jam 1:26 a person thinks he has reason for confidence or is religious: the thought is a self-trust the verse tests. In Heb 11:11 faith goes with the conceiving.
observations.grounds: the prudent gives thought to his steps

observations.text: In Heb 10:29 the hearers are asked to think how much worse a punishment the one deserves who has profaned the blood of the covenant: the thought is asked to weigh the profaning.
observations.grounds: How much worse punishment, do you think

observations.text: In Rom 12:3 Paul speaks by the grace given him when he tells them not to think too highly of themselves. In 2Cor 9:5 he thought it necessary that the gift be ready as a willing gift. In Heb 10:29 the one who outraged the Spirit of grace is the one the hearers are asked to think about.
observations.grounds: by the grace given to me I say to everyone

observations.text: In 2Sa 5:6 the Jebusites say the blind and lame will ward David off, thinking he cannot come in: blind is part of their boast, which their thought rests on.
observations.grounds: the blind and the lame will ward you off

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:16 and 2Cor 12:6 thinking is how others rate Paul, and boasting is what he weighs doing: let no one count him a fool, and he refrains from boasting so that no one thinks more of him than he sees.
observations.grounds: let no one think me foolish

observations.text: In 1Sa 18:17 Saul asks David to be valiant while he thinks to let the Philistines kill him: the call to courage hides the thought. In Job 32:6 Elihu was timid to declare his opinion. In Pro 21:29 the wicked puts on a bold face while the upright gives thought to his ways.
observations.grounds: A wicked man puts on a bold face

observations.text: In Gen 26:9 Abimelech calls Isaac and Isaac gives the thought behind his lie, and in 2Ki 5:11 Naaman thought the prophet would call on the Lord: call is the act the thought expected. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought Israel would call him Father, and in Jon 1:6 the captain urges Jonah to call on his god in the hope the god will give a thought to them. In Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 call is naming the child, with conceive in its bodily sense.
observations.grounds: And I thought you would call me, My Father

observations.text: In Deu 15:9 the people are to take care lest an unworthy thought be in the heart: the thought is what is to be guarded against. In Luk 8:18 take care is how to hear, and what one thinks he has may be taken. In Mat 22:16 care and opinion name Jesus not regarding a person's standing.
observations.grounds: Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart

observations.text: In Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 the thoughts alarm and the color changes: the change of face goes with the alarming thoughts, and in Dan 5:10 the queen bids the king's color not change. In Dan 7:25 the one against the Most High thinks to change the times and the law: there the change is what the thought intends.
observations.grounds: his thoughts alarmed him

observations.text: In Psa 50:21 the people thought God was like themselves because he was silent, and he now rebukes them: the false thought about God is met by his rebuke.
observations.grounds: you thought that I was one like yourself

observations.text: In Pro 15:26 the thoughts of the wicked stand against gracious words that are pure. In Phili 4:8 whatever is pure is among what the believers are to think on: the thinking is directed to purity.
observations.grounds: whatever is pure, whatever is lovely

observations.text: In 1Sa 18:17 Saul tells David to fight the Lord's battles while he thinks to let the Philistines kill him: the fighting is the cover of the thought. In 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 the Rabshakeh asks whether they think mere words are strategy for war. In Mic 2:8 with no thought of war renders a turning back, not a thought.
observations.grounds: Only be valiant for me and fight

observations.text: In Psa 119:52 thinking of the Lord's rules from of old brings comfort: the remembering is the ground of the comfort. In Job 12:5 the thought of one at ease holds contempt for misfortune: ease shapes the thought.
observations.grounds: When I think of your rules from of old, I take comfort

observations.text: In Num 36:6 the Lord commands that the daughters marry whom they think best within the clan: their judgment is free inside the command. In 1Ch 29:18 David asks the Lord to keep such thoughts in the hearts of his people and direct their hearts. In Psa 50:21 the Lord lays the charge before those who thought him like themselves. In Rom 12:3 sober thinking is by the measure God has assigned, and in 1Cor 14:37 the one who thinks he is spiritual is to acknowledge the Lord's command.
observations.grounds: Let them marry whom they think best

observations.text: In Phili 4:8 whatever is worthy of praise is among what the believers are to think about: the thinking is turned to what is commendable.
observations.grounds: if there is anything worthy of praise

observations.text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man is to forsake his thoughts and return to the Lord, who will have compassion on him: forsaking the thoughts opens the way to mercy. In Pro 15:26 gracious words stand against the thoughts of the wicked.
observations.grounds: the unrighteous man his thoughts

observations.text: In 1Ti 3:7 the overseer must be well thought of by outsiders: the requirement is a good report from others, not a thought of his own.
observations.grounds: he must be well thought of by outsiders

observations.text: In Gen 38:15 Judah took Tamar for a prostitute because she had covered her face: what is hidden leads the thought astray. In 2Ki 7:12 the king thinks the Syrians hide to trap them, and in Psa 64:5 the wicked lay snares secretly, thinking none will see. In Dan 2:30 and Luk 2:35 the thoughts are revealed: what is hidden in the heart is brought out.
observations.grounds: so that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed

observations.text: In Exo 2:14 Moses, asked who made him a judge, is afraid and thinks the thing is known. In Joh 5:45 the hearers are not to think Jesus will accuse them, for Moses does. In Jam 2:4 those who make distinctions become judges with evil thoughts: the judging is done from evil thoughts.
observations.grounds: become judges with evil thoughts

observations.text: In 1Cor 14:37 the one who thinks he is a prophet should acknowledge Paul's writing as the Lord's command: the self-view is tested by acknowledging. In Phili 3:15 where the mature think otherwise, God will reveal it to them.
observations.grounds: God will reveal that also to you

observations.text: In Gen 6:5 the thoughts of the heart are evil continually: the evil is lasting. In 1Sa 27:12 Achish thinks David will always be his servant, and in Joh 5:39 the hearers think they have eternal life in the Scriptures: the thought claims a lasting state the verse shows otherwise.
observations.grounds: only evil continually

observations.text: In Rom 14:14 Paul is persuaded nothing is unclean in itself, yet it is unclean to the one who counts it so: the thought makes it unclean for him. In 2Cor 10:5 every thought is taken captive to obey Christ: the thought is brought to obedience.
observations.grounds: unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean

observations.text: In Gen 6:5 the wickedness of man is great, and the thoughts of his heart are only evil: the wickedness seen on earth and the evil of the thoughts are named together.
observations.grounds: the wickedness of man was great in the earth

observations.text: In Job 15:35 and Isa 59:4 the wicked conceive mischief and their womb prepares deceit, with lies spoken. In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are just against the deceitful counsels of the wicked. In 1Cor 3:18, Gal 6:3 and Jam 1:26 the one who thinks himself wise, something or religious deceives himself, and in 2Cor 11:3 the thoughts may be led astray by deceit as Eve was.
observations.grounds: he deceives himself
